title: Joe Steele plays 'Rhapsody in Blue' for Gershwin
summary: Holmes relates hearsay that Steele played the whole Rhapsody at an audition for the show 'Rhapsody in Black' and Gershwin said he needed no instruction.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now, you said at one time that he played "Rhapsody in Blue" for Gershwin.

Well, they were putting on a show. "Rhapsody In Black" was the name of the show. An all-Negro show. And Gershwin provided the music. So they were using Gershwin's "Rhapsody In Blue" in the show. Now, this goes way back to the early Twenties, and "Rhapsody In Blue" at that time was not so popular -- it was just beginning to get known.

So they sent for Joe Steele to make an audition to play the Rhapsody to be used in the show, and Gershwin was there, amongst other nobility of the music world. So Joe comes in and he sits at the piano, and the conductor gives him the go-ahead signal. So the band started off, and Joe sits at the piano -- and he went all through the Rhapsody, beginning to end. And when they got through, Joe got a big hand from all the commentators standing around, musicians and one thing or another.
So Lew Leslie, the head of the show, this show, he was
the leader of the show, he told Joe, Joe Steele, to stand aside and...
Yeah... I'm trying to think of his first name.

That's right. That's a weird name. He told Joe to sit down, and George Gershwin would explain to him just what was what and how it was really supposed to go. So Gershwin heard Lew Leslie make that remark, and he said to Lew Leslie and everybody else standing around there...he said, "Well, there's nothing I can tell this man about playing 'Rhapsody.' He played it perfectly. There's nothing to tell him." Well, I mean, that was the big feather in the cap of Joe Steele, I mean, to have somebody like Gershwin make a remark like that about him the first time he sat down to play the music... "Rhapsody In Blue" was nothing easy to sit right down and play. And he played it right off, just like it's supposed to be done, and Gershwin was right there, and said there was nothing he could tell him.
Now, was this just the piano, or was it with an orchestra?
Do you remember who took the clarinet parts?
Oh, no. I don't know... I wasn't even there!
I see. You just heard about it.
I heard about it. Because you know, things like that, they have a way of getting out to the musicians.
